maria: Heads-up: after today's runtime merge (r3456) we're seeing a p95 warm-start spike on short-seq chat (~250ms -> ~480ms). appears during warmstart / kernel handshake between fused-attn and kv-prefetch.
jonathan: I see the same in canary dashboards, +1. spike correlates with a long serial wait in the decode path.
lee: timeline? any flamegraphs or profiler snippets?
maria: quick profiler excerpt:
```
2026-02-14 10:12:34.123 CPU  Thread-7  fused_dispatch.cpp:142 cudaStreamSynchronize (180ms)
2026-02-14 10:12:34.305 GPU  Stream-12    kv_prefetch.cpp:78 enqueue_prefetch (2ms)
2026-02-14 10:12:34.308 CPU  Thread-7  decoder_scheduler.cpp:89 schedule_kernel (5ms)
```
maria: flamegraph link: https://internal.perf/reports/1759954321 - shows long serial region between fused dispatch and KV handshake.
priya: I'm starting a git bisect between r3452..r3456. r3454 landed the fused-op scheduler change — initial suspect.
jonathan: deploy-bot already flagged a canary hold :warning:
deploy-bot: Canary hold engaged for runtime-canary-27 due to p95 > 2x baseline. Incident ticket INF-2021 created.
lee: quick test: can we flip the runtime flag `enable_fused_handshake=false` in the canary to see if we regress back to baseline?
maria: toggled the flag in the canary manually, p95 dropped back to ~260ms within 2m. seems to confirm handshake path regression.
priya: I'll open a revert PR for r3454 and continue bisect on an isolated branch to pinpoint commit. tagging @eng-oncall for coordination.
tom: note that reverting will touch dedicated CI. recommend schedule revert during low-traffic window and coordinate with infra.
maria: for now: hold rollout, canary rollback is active, bisect + perf runs in progress. i'll update INF-2021 and add profiler snapshots. :thumbsup:
